html:
SMTO-GWT-0050 — This Gateway is added by SMTO's startup settings and can't be deleted

GUID: 71edb29e-5d06-4299-864b-12b8b6aade46
Slug: gateway-startup-owned
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • This Gateway comes from the settings SMTO reads when it starts, so deleting it here wouldn't last; it would be added back the next time SMTO starts. Nothing was deleted or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway marked Startup configuration, and switch it Off in the Enabled column. A Gateway that is Off stays in the list but isn't offered for new Tasks, which is usually what deleting it was meant to do.
  2. If the switch can't be changed, expand the Gateway and read the note that lists the Tasks, runs, schedules or monitors still using it. Finish, stop or move that work first. SMTO won't turn off a Gateway that running or scheduled work still depends on.
  3. To remove the Gateway for good, ask the person who installed SMTO to take it out of SMTO's startup settings and then restart SMTO. Those startup settings are where this Gateway comes from, so that is the only place it can be removed permanently.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Off in Settings › Setup › Gateways and is no longer offered when you start a new Task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't try to remove the Gateway by editing SMTO's saved data files; change the startup settings instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway delete was refused because the registry record has source 'config': it is seeded from server startup configuration (AOR_GATEWAY_URL/AOR_DEFAULT_NODE or gateway_endpoints), which would recreate it.

What this means

  • Delete admission found that the Gateway record originated in server startup configuration, which would continue to define the entry. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Delete admission found that the Gateway record originated in server startup configuration, which would continue to define the entry.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the record's source and startup configuration, plus any active references that independently restrict disabling it.

How to fix it

  • Disable the record instead (the Enabled switch in Settings › Setup › Gateways, which is refused while tasks, runs, schedules or monitors still reference it), or remove its node from the Server's startup configuration (AOR_GATEWAY_URL / AOR_DEFAULT_NODE environment variables or the gateway_endpoints setting) and restart the Server. Startup seeding only inserts missing configuration entries, so confirm the existing record's state afterwards instead of assuming it was dropped.
  • Disable the entry through its existing control or edit the startup configuration to remove it permanently.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The startup-owned entry is deliberately disabled or removed from its owning configuration through a supported change.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
